title: Songwriting course learning map
scope: All 49 existing lessons mapped once; foundation units are teaching responsibilities and do not imply 21 new articles. Proposed dependencies describe comprehension before examples, not enforced navigation.

blocks.title: Start and listen
blocks.outcome: Recognize, capture and describe a musical idea.

blocks.title: Rhythm and groove
blocks.outcome: Explain a beat placement before hearing a syncopated or swung song passage.

blocks.title: Notes keys and chords
blocks.outcome: Build a palette, hear home and basic harmony, then finish the first miniature.

blocks.title: Melody and development
blocks.outcome: Repeat, shape and develop a recognizable musical thought.

blocks.title: Harmonic movement and colour
blocks.outcome: Choose voice motion, added colour or tonal change for a defined effect.

blocks.title: Words and musical meaning
blocks.outcome: Connect speaker, images, stress and developing meaning.

blocks.title: Layers and sound
blocks.outcome: Assign roles and distinguish a new sound from a new musical relationship.

blocks.title: Sections and the whole song
blocks.outcome: Give sections jobs, organize contrast and return, and shape the whole trajectory.
blocks.route: Core with optional verse and bridge lessons

blocks.title: Revise and finish
blocks.outcome: Identify one useful revision, make a clear version and finish.

foundations.title: Sound and musical roles
foundations.outcome: Separate pitch, loudness and timbre; distinguish a musical part from the instrument playing it.
foundations.first_visual: Briefly compare one note on two sounds and one sound at two pitches.

foundations.title: Pulse and tempo
foundations.outcome: Keep a pulse and distinguish faster tempo from more activity.
foundations.first_visual: Change tempo with the event pattern fixed.

foundations.title: Beats and bars
foundations.outcome: Count beat groups; distinguish beat division from bar grouping.
foundations.first_visual: Regroup six small pulses as three pairs or two threes.

foundations.title: Durations subdivisions and rests
foundations.outcome: Read or hear relative durations, silence and ties; account for a full bar.
foundations.first_visual: Keep one bar fixed while replacing an attack with a rest.

foundations.title: Even and uneven beat divisions
foundations.outcome: Hear straight versus unequal pairs; distinguish subdivision changes from shifting a whole part.
foundations.first_visual: Keep the beat steady and change only the second attack in each pair.

foundations.title: Pitch steps and intervals
foundations.outcome: Hear high and low; locate half steps, whole steps, octaves and register; compare contour with exact distances.
foundations.first_visual: Compare a moved phrase with a phrase whose last interval changes.

foundations.title: Major and natural minor scales
foundations.outcome: Build a note palette from a step pattern; distinguish a scale run from a phrase using that palette.
foundations.first_visual: Use the same tonic and rhythm to compare major with natural minor.

foundations.title: Tonal home and key relationships
foundations.outcome: Hear a tonic; distinguish scale collection from key, relative from parallel, and an altered note from a new home.
foundations.first_visual: Compare C major with A minor and with C minor using clear bass and endings.

foundations.title: Chord roots qualities and layouts
foundations.outcome: Build major and minor triads; distinguish root, bass, voicing and block versus broken presentation.
foundations.first_visual: Sound C E G separately then together; change only E to E-flat.

foundations.title: Scale degrees and chord numbers
foundations.outcome: Distinguish note degree 5 from chord V; recognize major and minor chord qualities in a key.
foundations.first_visual: Move I IV V to another key while keeping chord relationships.

foundations.title: Key signatures and the circle of fifths
foundations.outcome: Read neighboring signatures and relative key pairs; distinguish map distance from a chord progression.
foundations.first_visual: Add one sharp or flat at a time; separately show Dm G C root motion.

foundations.title: Progression arrival and harmonic rhythm
foundations.outcome: Hear chord succession, duration, arrival and open continuation; treat functional cadence as one possibility.
foundations.first_visual: Keep the melody fixed while changing only the final chord or chord-change timing.

foundations.title: Motif phrase and return
foundations.outcome: Distinguish a short cell from a phrase and a section; hear continuation, breath and return.
foundations.first_visual: Mark one cell inside a short phrase before naming larger song sections.

foundations.title: Voices bass and spacing
foundations.outcome: Follow individual lines; distinguish root from the lowest sounding note and voice leading from inversion.
foundations.first_visual: Hold two upper notes through a chord change while the bass moves separately.

foundations.title: Sevenths added notes and suspensions
foundations.outcome: Distinguish a seventh from an added note and a suspension from a replacement third.
foundations.first_visual: Change one note over a fixed triad and compare each chord label.

foundations.title: Speech stress syllables and rhyme
foundations.outcome: Hear natural speech stress and vowel sounds; distinguish syllable count from musical emphasis.
foundations.first_visual: Speak then sing the same short original line with two stress placements.

foundations.title: Texture timbre register and dynamics
foundations.outcome: Distinguish one line, doubling, accompaniment and independent lines; separate density, loudness and register.
foundations.first_visual: Hold notes fixed while changing roles or sound, then hold sound fixed while changing density.

foundations.title: Section roles and whole song form
foundations.outcome: Distinguish section roles and formal models from reusable techniques; compare sectional, developmental and process-driven perspectives without treating them as exclusive.
foundations.first_visual: A proportional whole-piece map, then optional layers and measured note activity; compare constant texture with layered entry over an unchanged figure.

foundations.title: Reading the displayed music
foundations.outcome: Connect piano-roll height and width to staff pitch, note duration, rests, clefs and key signatures when notation is selected.
foundations.first_visual: Switch one short original phrase between roll and score; label equivalent events.

foundations.title: Shared span and competing divisions
foundations.outcome: Hear three equal attacks against two over the same span; distinguish this from syncopation, triplets in one line and polymeter.
foundations.first_visual: Keep a common start and end and show 3 against 2 on aligned lanes.

foundations.title: Two lines and their vertical intervals
foundations.outcome: Follow each melody alone and together; notice register, rests and simultaneous intervals.
foundations.first_visual: Introduce a plain second line that answers and sometimes overlaps the first.

lessons.title: Protect the Song's Identity
lessons.handling: Keep; introduce listening roles before naming instruments.

lessons.title: Begin with What You Have
lessons.handling: Keep; use ordinary terms and sound-first entrances.

lessons.title: Listen Like a Songwriter
lessons.handling: Keep; separate heard observation from an analytical claim.

lessons.title: Capture Musical Seeds
lessons.handling: Keep; capture a seed without requiring notation.

lessons.title: Set the Pace for the Phrase
lessons.handling: Present pulse and tempo first; composing at a different pace is the application.

lessons.title: Group the Beat Around the Phrase
lessons.handling: Present beat grouping before choosing a meter.

lessons.title: Make Space Part of the Rhythm
lessons.handling: Separate duration and rest vocabulary from the pattern of using silence.

lessons.title: Pull an Entrance Across the Beat
lessons.handling: Keep syncopation and anticipation distinct; show expectation before displaced attacks.

lessons.title: Give the Groove a Consistent Feel
lessons.handling: Explain unequal pairs before swing; separately show whole-part timing.

lessons.title: Interlock the Groove
lessons.handling: Keep interlocking as an allocation of entrances and gaps.
lessons.first_visual: aligned drum bass and melody lanes

lessons.title: Intervals and Melodic Shape
lessons.handling: Retain the new foundation framing; interval preservation belongs to transposition.

lessons.title: Build a Scale from Steps
lessons.handling: Keep major and natural minor construction explicit before repertoire.

lessons.title: Establish a Tonal Home
lessons.handling: Keep establishing home as a choice; bring relative and parallel comparison forward from borrowing.
lessons.first_visual: same collection with different tonal anchors

lessons.title: Choose Chords by Their Notes
lessons.handling: Separate chord construction from later arpeggiation as an accompaniment pattern.
lessons.first_visual: stacked tones and block versus broken order

lessons.title: Think in Chord Numbers
lessons.handling: Teach degree numbers and Roman chord numbers as different labels.
lessons.first_visual: scale degree row linked to chord family row

lessons.title: Transpose the Song to Fit the Voice
lessons.handling: Split teaching into a key-map foundation then transposition; no need to create two articles immediately.

lessons.title: Decide Where the Harmony Arrives
lessons.handling: Introduce progression, cadence and harmonic rhythm before comparing endings.

lessons.title: Finish a Tiny Song
lessons.handling: Move after basic rhythm and harmony; its current sixteen-bar chord example assumes both.
lessons.first_visual: sixteen-bar opening answer contrast return map

lessons.title: Repeat with a Reason
lessons.handling: Place with motif development; show repetition at several musical scales.

lessons.title: Start with a Motif
lessons.handling: Keep motif identity audible; a motif can be rhythmic or timbral.

lessons.title: Give the Melody a Destination
lessons.handling: Keep contour as a compositional destination; introduce vocal range only when relevant.

lessons.title: Support or Challenge the Melody Note
lessons.handling: Explain stable chord tone and non-chord tone in this context before reharmonizing.
lessons.first_visual: held melody over two chord alternatives

lessons.title: Let the Phrase Breathe
lessons.handling: Move basic cell-versus-phrase vocabulary earlier; retain breathing and phrase length here.

lessons.title: Write a Hook
lessons.handling: Keep hooks distinct from motifs: a foreground identity or memory role.
lessons.first_visual: same texture with different foreground feature

lessons.title: Develop Without Losing the Idea
lessons.handling: Separate exact transposition from a diatonic sequence; label fragmentation and extension.

lessons.title: Connect Chords with Small Moves
lessons.handling: Define voice, bass, voicing and inversion before small-motion comparisons.

lessons.title: Write a Bass Line
lessons.handling: Keep bass as a melodic and rhythmic line; root motion alone is one variant.
lessons.first_visual: bass path beneath fixed upper harmony

lessons.title: Add Color to a Working Chord
lessons.handling: Stage seventh, added-note and suspension vocabulary in small comparisons.
lessons.first_visual: one changed chord tone in fixed voicing

lessons.title: Borrow a Chord
lessons.handling: Require parallel-versus-relative understanding before the borrowed chord example.
lessons.first_visual: same root and one altered third

lessons.title: Point to a Temporary Home
lessons.handling: Introduce dominant and leading-tone function locally before a secondary dominant; distinguish temporary emphasis from a new key.
lessons.first_visual: target chord with and without its approach

lessons.title: Change the Tonal World Deliberately
lessons.handling: Split mode and drone choices from modulation; preserve center versus establish a new center are different decisions.
lessons.first_visual: fixed center with changed palette then a new sustained center

lessons.title: Find the Central Idea
lessons.handling: Keep central lyrical situation independent of harmony prerequisites.

lessons.title: Choose the Speaker
lessons.handling: Keep speaker and addressee distinct; no music-theory gate.

lessons.title: Write Through Images
lessons.handling: Keep concrete images tied to action and viewpoint.
lessons.first_visual: abstract line and concrete original alternative

lessons.title: Let Sound Support the Lyric
lessons.handling: Introduce heard rhyme and vowel sound before choosing a scheme.

lessons.title: Make Speech and Melody Agree
lessons.handling: Use spoken emphasis before comparing musical stress.

lessons.title: Make the Lyric Develop
lessons.handling: Keep lyric development distinct from adding a new verse label.

lessons.title: Choose the World Around the Song
lessons.handling: Introduce texture and timbre before comparing sonic settings; cross-link early sound primer.
lessons.first_visual: same musical events in two sonic settings

lessons.title: Give Each Part a Job
lessons.handling: Make role and register distinct from instrument labels; point toward optional independent lines.

lessons.title: Let the Voice Carry the Meaning
lessons.handling: Vocal branch; distinguish doubling from harmony and check notes against chords.
lessons.first_visual: lead double and independent harmony lanes

lessons.title: Give Each Section a Purpose
lessons.handling: Define section role before a song diagram; distinguish refrain from chorus.

lessons.title: Make the Chorus Arrive
lessons.handling: Keep chorus lift multidimensional; harmony and loudness are optional ways.
lessons.first_visual: selected contrast at a section boundary

lessons.title: Make the Second Verse Count
lessons.handling: Keep second-verse development conditional on a form with verses.
lessons.first_visual: same section frame with new information

lessons.title: Earn the Bridge
lessons.handling: Keep bridge optional; contrast is useful only if it changes the return.
lessons.first_visual: return with and without a contrasting section

lessons.title: Choose a Form That Serves the Song
lessons.handling: Keep the existing canonical form-choice pattern. Introduce three overlapping perspectives; explain binary, ternary, AABA, theme and variations and through-composed development as models, with existing techniques cross-linked.
lessons.first_visual: Whole-piece timeline with original constant-texture versus layered-entry comparison; four windows are not automatically four sections.

lessons.title: Shape the Approach and the Ending
lessons.handling: Keep transition and ending choices connected to the whole approach.

lessons.title: Shape Energy over Time
lessons.handling: Keep the canonical energy pattern; develop Build by Layered Entry as a named technique. Explain changed/invariant/effect/use and distinguish measured note activity from perceived intensity.
lessons.first_visual: Proportional stage map with optional layer entrances and note-onset activity, following the existing audio clock.

lessons.title: Revise the Weakest Moment
lessons.handling: Keep diagnosis before intervention; the needed theory depends on the selected problem.
lessons.first_visual: one local change inside the whole song

lessons.title: Finish and Learn
lessons.handling: Keep finishing a decision and reflection process.

gaps.title: Apply the concept before example sequence across the course
gaps.evidence: The three guided pilots have concept openings. The shared article route still inserts the general player before article prose for other musical lessons.
gaps.action: Use the required foundation and first visual fields as a pre-example check for every lesson. Apply the new sequence before expanding the repertoire.

gaps.title: Move the first miniature
gaps.evidence: The chapter uses bars, quarter-note durations, chord symbols and chord-tone relationships before chapters 7–19 introduce them.
gaps.action: Place it after the basic notes-and-chords block; retain an optional unlabelled listening preview at the start.

gaps.title: Teach relative and parallel keys together
gaps.evidence: Relative keys appear in tonal home, while the explicit parallel distinction is developed later inside Borrow a Chord.
gaps.action: Put a C-major/A-minor/C-minor comparison before borrowing; do not claim minor scales themselves are missing.

gaps.title: Separate the key map from transposition
gaps.evidence: The circle chapter teaches signatures, relatives, fifth-root movement and whole-song transposition together.
gaps.action: Give the map its own foundation section, then use transposition as the composition or arrangement decision.

gaps.title: Develop arpeggiation as a pattern
gaps.evidence: A block-versus-broken chord comparison exists, but designing an arpeggiated accompaniment has no dedicated treatment.
gaps.action: Develop an optional pattern after triads plus duration and subdivision; hold harmony fixed while changing order, register and rhythm.

gaps.title: Add an independent-lines branch
gaps.evidence: Voice leading and arrangement roles offer seeds, but countermelody, contrary motion and imitation have no developed dedicated treatment.
gaps.action: Introduce independence and simultaneous intervals, then countermelody; add contrary motion and delayed imitation as separate patterns.

gaps.title: Add polyrhythm after shared time is secure
gaps.evidence: Triplets and compound subdivision are explained, but simultaneous contrasting divisions are not a developed lesson.
gaps.action: Introduce shared span and 3-against-2; contrast syncopation, triplet rhythm, polyrhythm and polymeter.

gaps.title: Split choices inside tonal-world changes
gaps.evidence: Modes, drones, tonicization, transposition and modulation describe several different operations.
gaps.action: Use a short comparison foundation, then separate keep-the-center/change-the-palette from establish-a-new-home; treat drone as a technique.

gaps.title: Strengthen the sound and texture route
gaps.evidence: A sonic-setting article and role-based arrangement exist, but the broader collection review finds timbral transformation, space and sampling thin or missing.
gaps.action: Introduce sound-versus-note and role vocabulary early. Keep sound-led composition as an expansion branch beyond this songwriting core.

gaps.title: Explain the score when notation is selected
gaps.evidence: The course offers notation views and a reading guide, but no staged pitch-and-rhythm bridge into staff reading.
gaps.action: Add an optional linked reading guide for clefs, rests, ties and key signatures. Staff fluency is not a gate for composing or hearing the concept.

gaps.title: Make the cell phrase section distinction explicit
gaps.evidence: Motif and phrase vocabulary is spread across miniature, motif and breathing chapters.
gaps.action: Introduce a short hierarchy before the miniature, then reuse the same terms in development and whole-form lessons.

extensions.title: Arpeggiation
extensions.move: Distribute a stable chord through time to create motion without changing the harmony.

extensions.title: Polyrhythms
extensions.move: Layer different equal divisions of the same time span while keeping their common cycle audible.

extensions.title: Countermelody
extensions.move: Give a second line its own contour and breathing while preserving a clear relationship with the main line.

extensions.title: Contrary Motion
extensions.move: Let two lines move in opposite directions; inspect the vertical intervals that result.

extensions.title: Imitation
extensions.move: Bring a recognizable idea into a second line after a delay while the first continues.

sources.title: Open Music Theory Fundamentals
sources.supports: Vocabulary and scope for pitch rhythm scales keys intervals triads numbers and texture; not the proposed course order.

sources.title: Open Music Theory Minor Scales
sources.supports: Natural minor, relative and parallel relationships, and key signatures.

sources.title: Open Music Theory Counterpoint
sources.supports: A reference for an optional independent-lines branch, rather than a compulsory species-counterpoint course.

curriculum_integration.module_role: Six topic entry points into the existing route, not an additional lesson manifest.
